messages:
maria-nguyen: hey @support — FjordPay hitting lots of 429s from production around minute boundaries on the streaming endpoint (/v1/streams/open). They say it started after a client SDK update.
kevin-zhou: thanks — any customer request traces or example headers? 429s every minute sounds like a window alignment issue but could also be a keepalive/reconnect pattern.
maria-nguyen: pasted a short curl trace they sent. note the nconns and repeated Authorization refresh calls.

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/open
* Connected to api.redwood.ai
> POST /v1/streams/open HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> user-agent: fjordpay-sdk/2.3.1
> content-length: 34
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-rw-rpm-limit: 120
< x-rw-rpm-remaining: 0
< x-rw-window-start: 1769601180
< x-request-id: rq_01ABCD
```

maria-nguyen: they also provided partial app logs showing repeated short-lived sockets and token refresh every ~45s.

jen-oncall: couple hypotheses:
- SDK changed keepalive/reconnect logic so clients open many short streams instead of reusing.
- Auth refresh stampede when tokens are close to expiry, each client instance refreshes independently at same offset -> bursts.
- Edge proxy mis-map of tenant headers causing aggregated counters across tenants.

kevin-zhou: can we confirm if x-rw-rpm-* headers above are coming from edge or our rate service? If edge is returning remaining:0, then the edge has the sliding window state.

rate-limiter-bot: note: per-tenant RPM is enforced at the edge by default for streaming routes. If client uses many sockets with different connection IDs, RPM counts each new connection's initial requests.

sam-sre: asking runtime to turn on debug counters for tenant fjordpay for next 10 minutes (will capture per-conn and per-route counts). Use flag: runtime.debug.tenant=fjordpay

maria-nguyen: customer repro steps included — cron job that spins up 50 micro-workers every minute to open a stream, then they upgraded sdk and now workers do a short run and exit. That aligns with top-of-minute spikes.

kevin-zhou: suggested quick checks for customer:
- Check SDK version and whether it enables ephemeral-token refresh by default.
- Confirm whether connections are reused or recreated per task.
- Inspect client app logs for Authorization: fetch calls timestamps.

kevin-zhou: suggested mitigation steps to give the customer now:
1) increase SDK connection pool reuse (maxIdleConns) or reuse one stream per process.
2) if using token refresh, jitter refresh times across workers (random 0-30s offset) to avoid stampede.
3) enable client-side backoff on 429 and exponential jitter (don’t retry-blast on minute boundary).
4) request a temporary quota bump while they rollout fixes: please provide approximate peak RPS.

maria-nguyen: asked customer for peak numbers — they replied ~90 initial opens/minute across all regions, previously was ~10.

jen-oncall: internal ask -> eng-runtime: can we add per-route minute-bucket histogram for fjordpay + a trace for x-request-id rq_01ABCD so we can correlate connections that triggered the drop?

sam-sre: enabled debug for 15 minutes. pulled a short histogram:

```text
minute bucket 1769601180: 130 opens
minute bucket 1769601240: 12 opens
```

sam-sre: also found that many opens had identical User-Agent + same IP range -> looks like a scheduled worker fanout.

kevin-zhou: conclusion: customer-side fanout created minute-boundary alignment, hitting per-tenant RPM window. Edge returned 429 with x-rw-rpm-remaining:0. Not an internal bug but expected behavior given the quota.

maria-nguyen: forwarded mitigation guide to customer with concrete SDK changes and a suggested temporary quota increase to 250 RPM while they patch.

maria-nguyen: customer applied staggered start (randomized 0-60s) and increased reuse. After changes they reported 429s dropped to near zero.

jen-oncall: follow-up action for product docs: add a short note on streaming endpoints and RPM semantics + recommended client patterns (reuse connections, jitter token refresh, avoid minute-boundary schedules).

kevin-zhou: optional runtime enhancement: consider adding a soft-smoothing layer that can accept small bursts by smoothing counts across sliding window for streaming routes (needs product approval).

maria-nguyen: closing loop with customer — they thanked us, will keep quota bump for 48h and monitor. marking resolved.

sam-sre: noted for the postmortem: label as customer-side pattern (cron fanout + token refresh stampede) and doc/update checklist.

rate-limiter-bot: incident-tag: support/429-customer-fanout
